summary: Developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, Earth Jukebox is an inclusive web application that makes satellite observations of Earth—such as temperature, sea ice, marine life, and precipitation—accessible to blind and visually impaired individuals through data sonification. By dividing the planet into eight latitudinal bands mapped to a pentatonic scale (ranging from high-pitched at the North Pole to low-pitched at the South Pole) and scanning across longitudes from west to east with stereo spatialization, the tool translates the intensity of climate phenomena into distinct timbres, volumes, and subtle harmonic variations. Fully navigable via keyboard or touch, and featuring integrated text-to-speech, the application allows for isolation by latitude, temporal comparison of anomalies, and support for authentic NASA imagery (such as "Blue Marble" or "Earth at Night"). It also enables the import of custom images and the export of high-fidelity WAV audio files, transforming planetary science into a universal, rigorous, and moving sensory experience.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

Earth Jukebox is an accessible, web-based Earth observation sonification engine that translates global satellite imagery—from NASA’s Earth Information Center and Earth Observatory—into an intuitive, multi-voiced auditory experience for blind, visually impaired, and sighted users alike.

The Sonification Architecture:

  • 8-Latitude Polyphonic Grid: The globe is divided into eight equal horizontal latitude bands (from 90∘N90∘N to 90∘S90∘S). Each latitude corresponds to a dedicated voice tuned to a harmonious pentatonic scale, where high pitches represent polar/northern regions and deep bass notes represent the Antarctic/southern regions (784 Hz784 Hz [G5], 587.33 Hz587.33 Hz [D5], 440 Hz440 Hz [A4], 329.63 Hz329.63 Hz [E4], 261.63 Hz261.63 Hz [C4], 196 Hz196 Hz [G3], 146.83 Hz146.83 Hz [D3], and 110 Hz110 Hz [A2]).
  • Longitudinal Sound Sweep (180∘W→180∘E180∘W→180∘E): The application scans west-to-east across longitudes over a customizable duration (e.g., 8, 16, or 24 seconds). A subtle stereo panner node moves the acoustic field from the left ear to the right ear in real time.
  • Calibrated Scientific Chromatic Formula: To avoid false readings where bright colors (like desert sand or yellow highlights) overpower thermal extremes, the engine computes data intensity via a hue-weighted formula: Value=0.85×HueHeat(R,G,B)+0.15×LuminanceValue=0.85×HueHeat(R,G,B)+0.15×Luminance This guarantees that true thermal or climatic maximums (saturated reds/whites) sound louder than transitional yellows.
  • Tension Detuning & Acoustic Feedback: Values above $0.75$ (critical heatwaves, severe storms, or ocean bloom surges) introduce up to +50 cents+50 cents of intentional microtonal detuning and open a dynamic low-pass resonant filter (300–4800 Hz300–4800 Hz), conveying urgent environmental stress.
  • Geographical Landmarks & Dual Chimes: Soft acoustic chimes ring at major meridian intervals (180∘180∘, 90∘W90∘W, 90∘E90∘E), with a distinct double high chime (880 Hz+1320 Hz880 Hz+1320 Hz) identifying the Greenwich Prime Meridian (0∘0∘).
  • Real & Simulated Datasets: Users can explore four simulated procedural climatic baselines (Temperature, Sea Ice, Ocean Chlorophyll, Precipitation), authentic NASA Earth Observatory captures (Blue Marble and Earth at Night), or upload any custom GeoTIFF/PNG satellite map.
  • Interactive Exploration & WAV Export: Users can pause, isolate any single latitude band in "Solo" mode, inspect point anomalies in differential comparison mode (baseline vs. observed anomaly), listen to speech-synthesized summaries, and export high-fidelity 44.1 kHz 16-bit stereo WAV recordings.

2. What benefits does it bring?

  • True Universal Accessibility: Traditional Earth observation relies heavily on dense false-color heatmaps inaccessible to over 285 million blind and visually impaired individuals worldwide. Earth Jukebox unlocks direct, unmediated engagement with planetary health data.
  • Multimodal Cognitive Advantage: The human auditory cortex detects subtle temporal rhythms, micro-variations, and multi-layered trends faster than visual scanning can parse cluttered color bars.
  • Temporal Anomaly Detection: The differential comparison mode maps positive and negative anomalies into distinct acoustic timbres (rising tension for warming, deep grounding for cooling), highlighting climate shocks that can be missed visually.
  • Flexible Pedagogical Tool: Teachers, museum docents, and planetarium curators can isolate specific latitudes (e.g., Arctic sea ice vs. tropical convective belts) to demonstrate atmospheric mechanics without needing specialized GIS software.
  • Offline & Broadcast Ready: The integrated browser-side WAV audio renderer enables podcasters, educators, and science communicators to generate broadcast-ready audio clips directly from satellite feeds.

3. What is the expected impact?

  • In Science Education & Planetariums: Transforming passive observation into an evocative auditory journey where students literally "hear" the greenhouse effect, the retreat of polar caps, and the breathing of oceanic plankton.
  • For the Visually Impaired Community: Empowering blind students and citizen scientists to actively participate in STEM research, climate monitoring, and data interpretation with zero specialized hardware requirements.
  • In Climate Advocacy & Emotional Engagement: Climate change data is often perceived as abstract statistics or color-saturated charts. Hearing global temperature anomalies create audible harmonic dissonance elicits a direct visceral and emotional connection with planetary health.
  • Open Science & NASA Data Adoption: Providing an open-source bridge between raw satellite datasets and human sensory perception, accelerating public adoption of NASA's Earth Information Center initiatives.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Language & Core Framework: TypeScript (strict mode), React 19, and TanStack Start v1 with Vite for modern full-stack performance and edge optimization.
  • Audio Synthesis Engine: Native Web Audio API utilizing custom additive synthesizers (PeriodicWave), BiquadFilterNode, StereoPannerNode, DynamicsCompressorNode, and stereo ping-pong delay lines, operating with zero external audio bloatware.
  • Digital Audio Encoding: A zero-dependency, pure TypeScript PCM WAV encoder generating binary RIFF headers and 44.1 kHz, 16-bit signed integer stereo buffers (ArrayBuffer / DataView).
  • Image Processing & Computer Vision: HTML5 2D Canvas API for high-frequency pixel rasterization, color-space conversions (RGB to HSV/Luminance), and procedural fractal Perlin-noise simulation.
    • W3C ARIA live regions (aria-live="polite", role="region", role="status", focus rings).
    • Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesisUtterance) providing localized bilingual descriptions and end-of-sweep automated climate insights.
    • Navigator Vibration API for tactile haptic feedback during interactive touch scrubbing.
  • Styling & Design System: Tailwind CSS v4 featuring deep oceanic dark-mode tokens, high-contrast ratios ($>7:1$), minimum 44px touch targets, and full respect for prefers-reduced-motion.
  • Testing & Quality Assurance: Vitest and Playwright for unit and end-to-end testing of frequency maps, color-to-heat equations, accessibility navigation, and WAV output validation.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Musical Harmony as a Scientific Language: Instead of unpleasant, fatigue-inducing Geiger-counter clicks or harsh beeps, we adopted a soft pentatonic harmonic lattice with three switchable acoustic personas (Cosmic Pad, Ambient Chime, and Pure Scientific). The auditory space remains comfortable and musical even during long analytical listening sessions.
  • Spatial Geography: By binding orbital longitude to binaural stereo panning and latitude to pitch height, the listener develops a spatial cognitive mental map of the Earth—instinctively identifying whether a heatwave is centered over the Pacific, the Sahara, or the Indian Ocean.
  • Harmonic Dissonance as an Alarm: Rather than relying on volume alone, climatic anomalies introduce acoustic friction (detuning in cents). The planet sounds "healthy" and consonant under balanced conditions, and audibly "strained" when greenhouse thresholds are breached.
  • Closed-Eyes Discovery: Sighted participants who test the app with their eyes closed frequently report spotting the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) or the Saharan heat belt faster through their ears than they did visually on a traditional 2D map.

6. What factors did your team take into account?

  • Cognitive Load & Auditory Fatigue: Playing eight simultaneous polyphonic voices for prolonged periods can overwhelm the ear. We engineered a dedicated Latitude Solo mode, dynamic soft compression to prevent clipping, and an acoustic low-pass ceiling to eliminate harsh high-frequency harmonics.
  • Scientific Calibration vs. Human Vision Bias: Human retinas perceive yellow as brighter than red, even though thermal datasets treat red as the hottest index. Our colorimetric engine applies an HSV hue-distance weighting algorithm to ensure scientific accuracy in acoustic representation.
  • Zero Barrier to Entry: The app requires no login, no downloads, and runs entirely in any modern browser on smartphones, tablets, or desktop screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver).
  • International Inclusivity: Full bilingual support (English and French), with dynamically translated interfaces, keyboard shortcuts, and synthesized voice announcements.
  • Strict Consent-Based Audio: Respecting browser audio autoplay policies and user agency, sound synthesis is never triggered automatically on page load; it requires an explicit user action (button tap or spacebar keystroke).
  • Low-Bandwidth & Resilient Architecture: Designed to work efficiently even on constrained mobile networks or offline after initial load, without relying on heavy cloud inference or external audio streaming servers.
